llcFilesWith: Michigan Department of Licensing and Regulatory Affairs (LARA), Corporations, Securities & Commercial Licensing Bureau (Certificate of Assumed Name, Form CSCL/CD-541, MCL 450.4206)
soleProprietorFilesWith: County clerk of each county where the business is conducted (sole proprietors and general partnerships file an assumed name / co-partnership certificate under the county assumed name law)
feeBasis: The LARA fee for an LLC's Certificate of Assumed Name is $25. Sole proprietors pay the county clerk's fee, which varies by county.
duration: Through December 31 of the fifth full calendar year after filing
renewalRule: An LLC's assumed name expires on December 31 of the fifth full calendar year following the year it was filed, and may be extended for further consecutive five-year periods by filing a renewal certificate no earlier than 90 days before expiration. LARA must notify the company of the impending expiration at least 90 days out (MCL 450.4206(2), (3)).
protectionNote: An assumed name lets a company trade under a different name; it is disclosure, and although it is part of the LARA name screen, it is not a trademark and grants no exclusive market right. MCL 450.4206(4) says so directly, and (5) goes further: two or more companies operating together in a partnership or joint venture may each file the same assumed name, so a Michigan assumed name is not even exclusive on the register.
searchNote: Assumed names filed by LLCs and corporations appear in the LARA business entity search. County-level assumed names for sole proprietors sit in county clerk records.
notes: Michigan splits its DBA system. An LLC files a Certificate of Assumed Name with LARA ($25, MCL 450.4206); the assumed name expires on December 31 of the fifth full calendar year following the year of filing and renews for five-year periods, with a 90-day pre-expiry filing window and a matching 90-day LARA notice. Sole proprietors and general partnerships instead file an assumed name with the county clerk. The LARA assumed name is part of the entity-name screen (MCL 450.4206(1) lets a company use an assumed name only if it is not precluded under section 204(3)), so it can block a later LLC name, but it grants no exclusive right and needs no publication.
